title: Redwood PLG Quickstart - Discovery - Aurora Ventures
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
summary: AE+SE intro call covering Aurora Ventures' interest in Redwood's PLG quickstart and options for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer is evaluating time-to-first-token, integration work (SDK/curl), security controls (SOC2, KMS, VPC), and baseline cost/latency. Action items: send quickstart guide and credits, schedule infra deep dive, prepare benchmarking plan for 1M tokens/day, share SOC2 and KMS docs.
next_steps: Samira to send quickstart guide + free credits details (via email)
Schedule 60-min technical deep dive with Aurora infra team (Diego + Marcus)
Share SOC2 report and KMS integration guide
Provide Dedicated pricing options and estimated performance
action_items: Samira Patel: Email quickstart guide, sample curl, and promo free credits (2026-04-19)
Diego Ramos: Draft benchmarking plan for 1M tokens/day and proposed test cases (2026-04-22)
Marcus Chen: Share current infra diagram and throughput targets (2026-04-20)
Priya Nair: Confirm network constraints and VPC peering requirements (2026-04-21)
transcript: [00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — i'm Samira from Redwood, AE on the account. Diego is our solutions engineer. How are you all?

[00:08] Lena: Hi Samira, thanks. i'm lena. we've been poking around the Redwood quickstart but wanted to chat about next steps and whether we can move fast with the hosted api vs dedicates or a private deployment.
[00:20] Diego: Great, quick context question — what's your current stack for model serving? are you running internal transformer endpoints or using a managed provider?

[00:27] Marcus: We're mostly internal today, triton + k8s, a mix of fp16 on p4s. We also have a small prod cluster for embeddings. Chief concern is cost predictability and also getting to first token quickly for a POC.

[00:39] Samira: Totally. The PLG quickstart flows are designed for fast time-to-first-token — sign up, api key, run the sample curl or sdk and you can get tokens in minutes. We also offer free credits for trial POCs.
[00:51] Lena: When you say minutes — is that like 5–15 min? any common gotchas?

[00:56] Diego: Typically 5–20 min depending on onboarding and if you want to pin a model. Often the slow part is SSO or org setup if you want RBAC or dedicated billing. But for pure hosted api it's very quick — key, install sdk, test. We have a quickstart repo.
[01:12] Marcus: For security we need SOC2 and KMS integrations — we can't send PII to a third-party without encryption at rest keyed by us. What's the support for customer-managed keys?

[01:21] Samira: We support KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we offer encryption at rest with our managed keys, but we can discuss Bring Your Own Key for Dedicated and Private. We'll attach the SOC2 report and the KMS guide after the call.
[01:35] Priya: Also network — do you support VPC peering for private deployments? if we go Private we need peering and strict egress controls.

[01:41] Diego: Yes, Private includes VPC and on-prem options. Dedicated offers a tenant-isolated GPU pool and can be deployed in a customer VPC with peering. For the PLG quickstart you'll start hosted then we can evaluate Dedicated for predictability.
[01:55] Lena: Cost tradeoffs — we have a target of 1M tokens/day for the pilot, mostly chat responses. Any rough price/perf ballpark?

[02:02] Diego: Rough back-of-envelope depends on model choice and quantization. For an open LLM variant on Dedicated with int8 quant we often see 3–5x lower token cost vs naive self-hosting because of batching, KV cache and smart routing; but we'll run numbers. We'll draft a benchmarking plan for your 1M tokens/day scenario.
[02:18] Marcus: What about latency? our UX needs 150–300ms p50 for short responses, otherwise we see drop-off.

[02:23] Diego: For cached/short responses hosted can hit p50 ~80–200ms depending on model; Dedicated tuned runtime can provide tighter SLOs. Part of the deep dive we'll map expected latency at your target QPS and sequence lengths.
[02:35] Lena: For the quickstart i'm assuming we don't need any infra changes from your side? just dev keys and sdk?

[02:40] Samira: Correct — quickstart is self-serve. We'll send a sample curl plus SDK snippets (python/node) so your engineers can get tokens in a sandbox. We'll also include notes on streaming responses and function calling if you want structured outputs.
[02:53] Priya: Any limits on rate or quotas during the trial credits? we want to simulate production-like load.

[02:58] Samira: Trial credits come with a modest rate cap to prevent abuse, but we can lift limits for coordinated benchmarking with Diego's help. For full load you'll likely want a Dedicated trial or a benchmarking window.
[03:10] Marcus: We also need to understand audit logs and retention — auditors will ask where logs are stored and for how long.
[03:15] Samira: We have per-request tracing and retention options in Redwood Console; enterprise packages include extended retention and export to your SIEM. We'll include documentation.
[03:24] Lena: Great. i'd also like to validate the SDK integration with our backend — can you walk someone through a quick code path?

[03:30] Diego: Yes, we can do a technical walkthrough. Plan would be: quickstart steps for devs, then a 60-min deep dive where we map your endpoints, auth flow, and run a small benchmark. I'll prepare the test harness.
[03:42] Marcus: One question — you mentioned model variants and fallbacks. Does Redwood route to smaller models automatically to save cost?

[03:49] Diego: We support smart routing policies. You can prioritize latency or cost; we can route by policy and fallback to compatible model variants. It's configurable per-route. Sometimes the docs show 'Redwood Dedicate' or 'Redwood Private'— apologies for the auto transcript — but yes the runtime supports that.
[04:05] Lena: Any typical blockers you see in other customers moving from quickstart to Dedicated?

[04:09] Samira: SLA and compliance reviews take time — SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, and network peering are the usual gatechecks. Also pricing approvals for reserved capacity. We try to parallelize security review while your engineers test the hosted quickstart.
[04:22] Marcus: Sounds good. let's do the hosted quickstart now and schedule the deep dive. Who will own sending the credits and docs?
[04:27] Samira: I'll send the quickstart guide, credits, sample curl and the SOC2 + KMS doc by tomorrow. Diego will set up the benchmark plan and we'll coordinate times for the 60-min deep dive.
[04:35] Priya: Quick practical — do you have a sample curl we can paste into our infra for smoke tests?

[04:39] Diego: Yeah i'll include a curl and python snippet in the quickstart. Example: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' — small note: some customers typo the endpoint so watch the prefix.
[04:55] Lena: Perfect. Anything else?
[05:00] Samira: Recap: send quickstart + credits + security docs, schedule deep dive, benchmark plan. We'll follow up with Dedicated pricing options once we have throughput targets. Thanks everyone.
[05:08] Marcus: Thanks, appreciate it.
[05:11] Meeting ended
